messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] saturating 5xx on serving-runtime (region: us-west-2). Observed GPU node failure pattern: CUDA illegal memory access / misaligned address on gpu-node-42. Auto-escalating to #incidents. Logs: https://logs.redwood/trace/2469783456 :rotating_light:

maya: I'm oncall. Confirming -- saw a spike starting ~03:23 UTC, several containers OOMing then CUDA illegal memory. Taking node out of rotation now.

sam: copy of the kernel oops from node-42 attached below. looks like pagewalk/misaligned pointer in our custom memcopy kernel. suspect race between eviction + async prefetch.

sam: ```
[03:23:12Z] gpu0: illegal memory access at 0x7ffefc123450
Backtrace: gpu_kernel.cu:342 kernel_copy()
  kv_cache.cu:120 flush_kv_cache()
  runtime.cu:88 process_request()
[03:23:12Z] Container runtime OOM, pid 21456 terminated
```

liu: thanks. this matches earlier flaky repros we saw in staging with concurrent paging under burst. triggering emergency mitigation: 1) cordon+drain node-42, 2) pin traffic away from older kernel image, 3) fallback to quantized model variant on affected routes.

maya: executing cordon/drain now. @deploy-bot can you pause canary rollouts?

deploy-bot: Roger. Pausing canaries for model-serving and routing policies.

maya: ```sh
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-node-42
```

sam: after drain, we should restart the containerd on node-42 and collect full coredump and nvcrash. lmK to grab /var/crash and nvcrash logs. Also enable debug mem-trace on the small subset of replicas to reproduce safely.

liu: rolling traffic: switching model routes for <customer-facing-endpoints> to model-quant-v2 (32-bit quant) and enabling strict KV-cache bypass for new inferences. This should reduce async prefetch pressure. Routing change in console done, pushing now.

ashley: Support note: currently ~8 customers experienced failures (5xx) across sessions, largest impact is a PLG customer cluster (org id 8421). Opening incident tickets and adding postmortem flag. Customer-facing message drafted, awaiting @maya approval.

maya: approve the message, send with note we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.

pagerduty: paging summary: page sent to oncall at 03:24 UTC, handoff to backup at 03:36 UTC due to escalation.

sam: node-42 restart complete, nvcrash files: /var/log/nvcrash/2469783456.tgz uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-crash-logs/2469783456.tgz. core dump size ~1.2GB. nvtool trace shows misaligned access inside register spill region when sequence length > 2048.

liu: temporary mitigations in place:
- cordoned node drained and isolated
- model route fallback active (quant variant)
- canaries paused
- scaled up healthy pool in us-west-2 by +3 replicas

maya: customer impact contained, error rate back to baseline for most routes. Keeping this thread open for evidence collection and handoff to eng-runtime for RCA. @sam @liu please include the nvcrash and kernel oops dumps in the postmortem.

sam: noted. I'll open a bug (ENG-3971) linking logs + coredump + repro script. Initial hypothesis: kernel race during concurrent pagewalks + async eviction; high priority to reproduce with synthetic load.

liu: I'll run a focused repro on a spare node with kernel debug flags and reduced scheduling noise, try to reproduce address misalignment in our copy kernels. ETA 4 hours.

ashley: I posted a short customer update and ticket numbers: #INC-8421, #INC-8422. Marking as 'mitigated' in support tracker for now.

maya: leaving handoff notes for next oncall: 1) node-42 nvcrash tar in S3, 2) ENG-3971 created, 3) rollback still available in console under rollouts->serving-runtime, 4) follow up with customers in 2 hours.

liu: adding short checklist to ENG-3971 for reproducer, kernel configs, and potential quick patch (bounds checks in gpu memcpy).

maya: thanks team. I'll uncordon/return node to pool only after eng-runtime confirms fixes and we've run soak for 2 hours. Closing immediate mitigation in 30m unless regressions. :thumbsup:
